operationalSituations.description: cpp-FuSa runs as part of a CI pipeline gate before a merge or release is allowed to proceed.
cpp-FuSa's own evidence-generation commands (fmea/tara/hara/safety-case/sas/sci) are run to produce artifacts a certification reviewer will read as a record of the project's actual safety analysis.
A project author edits .fusa-hara.json, .fusa-dispositions.json, or .fusa.json directly to record hazard analysis, waive a finding, or configure the safety standard/ASIL cpp-FuSa is held to.

hazards.description: cpp-FuSa's `check` command fails to detect a genuine safety-relevant defect (a false negative in the engine/lint/analyze/cyber rule set), so defective code passes the CI gate believing the tool found nothing.
hazards.source: Design review of src/engine/engine.cpp — a rule that throws or silently returns no findings is indistinguishable from a rule that ran and found nothing.

hazards.description: A generated evidence artifact (fmea.json, tara.json, .fusa-hara.json, safety-case.json, sas.json) ships with untouched template/placeholder text or a single hardcoded qualitative string applied to every entry, and a certification reviewer mistakes it for genuine, item-specific analysis.
hazards.source: 2026-07-28 cross-tool content audit (x-FuSa spec §1.6) — found exactly this pattern in this repo's own .fusa-hara.json before the fix that accompanies this file.

hazards.description: hara::determine_asil's S x E x C lookup table (ISO 26262-3:2018 Table 4) contains a transcription error, so a hazard is assigned a lower ASIL than the standard actually requires.
hazards.source: Code review of src/hara/hara.cpp's hand-encoded Table 4 lookup — a static lookup table has no built-in cross-check against the published standard.

hazards.description: A disposition entry in .fusa-dispositions.json is added at rule-level scope (the only scope this tool's disposition mechanism currently supports) and silently suppresses every current and future finding for that rule project-wide, including ones the author did not intend to waive.
hazards.source: Design review of src/disposition/disposition.cpp — find_by_rule matches on ruleId alone, with no file/line/fingerprint granularity.

hazards.description: An evidence artifact carries a stale or self-attested §1.6.2 attestation (independentReviewer equal to implementationAuthor, or a contentHash left over from a prior version of the file), and a consumer trusts it as a genuine independent review.
hazards.source: Design review of src/quality/quality.cpp's is_valid_reviewed — an attestation object is only as trustworthy as the check that validates it.

safetyGoals.description: cpp-FuSa's check gate shall never report a clean result when a rule encountered an error or produced no findings due to a bug, so a defect is never mistaken for an absence of defects.
safetyGoals.safeState: A rule that errors surfaces as a WARNING/ERROR finding of its own (never silently swallowed), and `check` exits non-zero.

safetyGoals.description: Every generated evidence artifact with free-text qualitative content shall be scanned for placeholder text and blanket qualitative fallback before a reviewer sees it, and shall carry an honest attestation of its review status.
safetyGoals.safeState: FUSA-STUB001 always fires as an ERROR (disposition-suppressible only); FUSA-STUB002 fires as an advisory WARNING unless a valid attestation is present.

safetyGoals.description: cpp-FuSa's ASIL determination shall be independently verified against every cell of ISO 26262-3:2018 Table 4, not merely spot-checked, so a transcription error cannot silently under-classify a hazard.
safetyGoals.safeState: determine_asil is covered by an exhaustive S×E×C test matrix; any mismatch against the published table fails the test suite before release.

safetyGoals.description: A disposition waiver shall always carry an identified reviewer and rationale, and shall be visible in code review, so an overly broad rule-level waiver is a deliberate, auditable decision rather than an accident.
safetyGoals.safeState: disposition add requires --reviewer and --rationale; .fusa-dispositions.json changes go through the same PR review as any other change.

safetyGoals.description: An attestation shall only be treated as a valid independent review when the reviewer differs from the implementation author and the recorded content hash matches the artifact's current content; a stale or self-attested one shall fall back to heuristic.
safetyGoals.safeState: quality::is_valid_reviewed enforces both checks before FUSA-STUB002 is suppressed.
